Dated this the 30th day of September, 2024 This Criminal Miscellaneous Case has been filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, to quash all further proceedings pursuant to Annexure.A2 FIR and Annexure.A3 Final Report in C.C. No.298/2022 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-II, Palakkad.

sentences.text: The petitioners herein are accused Nos. 2 to 5 in the above case.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners, the learned Public Prosecutor and the learned counsel appearing for the defacto complainant, in detail.
Perused the Final Report and statement of the defacto complainant.

3. In this matter, the prosecution alleges commission of offences punishable under Sections 498(A)
read with 34 of IPC, by accused Nos. 1 to 5.
The 1 st accused is the husband of the defacto complainant.
The 2 nd accused is the mother of the 1 st accused.
Accused Nos. 3 and 4 are sisters of the 1st accused and the 5th accused is the 2024:KER:72715 2024:KER:588 husband of the 3 rd accused.

The prosecution allegation is that, the 1st accused married the defacto complainant on 26.05.2016 as per religious ceremonies and at the time of marriage, the parents of the defacto complainant entrusted 30 sovereigns of gold ornaments and Rs.50,000/- as marriage gift to her.

sentences.text: The sisters of the 1 st accused were married at the time of the marriage between the 1 st accused and the defacto complainant.

The allegation of the defacto complainant is that, on the date of marriage itself, during night, the sisters of the 1 st accused obtained her gold ornaments excluding one chain,
two bangles and earing.

Thereafter, the defacto complainant and the 1 st accused left to Bangalore,
where they had been working in the IT field.

The 2nd accused/1st petitioner herein also accompanied them and during their stay at Bangalore, the 2nd accused used to make problems on saying that there was a practice in Palakkad to give chain to the husband during marriage.
Thereafter, the parents of the defacto complainant given gold chain having 2.5 sovereigns to the 1st accused.

It is alleged further that, after the nodule 2024:KER:72715 2024:KER:588 surgery of the defacto complainant, the 2nd accused demanded more gold ornaments from the defacto complainant on asserting that the sisters of the 1 st accused were given 40 sovereigns of gold ornaments at the time of their marriage.
The allegation against the sisters are that, they used to persecute the defacto complainant, when they would come to the house.
The allegation against the 5 th accused is that, after the nodule surgery of the defacto complainant, he stated that the defacto complainant was abnormal and she could not become pregnant.

At the same time, the defacto complainant stated that, during November, 2020, the 1st accused beat her alleging that she did not have the required beauty and the gold given during marriage was insufficient.
4. According to the learned counsel for the petitioners, the allegations are false and the petitioners are innocent.
He would submit that, after one week of the marriage, the defacto complainant along with the 1 st accused went to Bangalore and they resided together at Bangalore.

Accused Nos. 3 and 4, sisters of the 1 st accused, 2024:KER:72715 2024:KER:588 who are admittedly married, were staying away from the matrimonial home and they had no occasion to persecute the defacto complainant, in any manner.
Similarly, the allegation against the 5 th accused also is omnibus, so as to implicate him in this crime.
He also would point out that, even though some allegations are raised against the mother of the 1st accused, who is the 2nd accused/1st petitioner herein, the same are not specific.
Therefore, the quashment prayer is liable to be allowed.

5. The prayer for quashment is zealously opposed by the learned counsel for the defacto complainant, reading out the overt acts at the instance of the accused, on the submission that the overt acts stated in the FIS by the defacto complainant are specific so as to warrant trial of the matter.

6. The learned Public Prosecutor, though supported the argument of the learned counsel for the defacto complainant as against the 2nd accused, he also would submit that the allegations against accused Nos. 3 to 5 are general in nature.

In order to address the rival contentions, reference to Section 498A of IPC is necessary, which reads as under:
"Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty - Whoever,
being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to Prasanna vs State Of Kerala on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39290669/
3
cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.

Explanation.--For the purposes of this section, "cruelty means"--
(a) anywilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand."
8. Going by the definition, subjecting a woman to 2024:KER:72715 2024:KER:588 cruelty by husband or relative of the husband likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman or harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coerce her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand, is an offence.

9. In the decision reported in Achin Gupta v. State of Haryana,[2024 KHC OnLine 6257 : 2024 (3)
KHC SN 24 : 2024 LiveLaw (SC) 343 : 2024 KLT OnLine 1481], the Apex Court considered earlier decisions of the Apex Court dealing with Section 498A of IPC and it was held that general and sweeping allegations without mentioning specific instances of criminal conduct is an abuse of the process of court and in such cases the courts owe a duty to subject the allegations levelled in the complaint to a thorough scrutiny to find out, prima facie, whether there is any grain of truth in the allegations or 2024:KER:72715 2024:KER:588 whether they are made only with the sole object of involving some individuals in a criminal charge, more particularly, when a prosecution arises from a matrimonial dispute.

sentences.text: 10. It is noticed that, in matrimonial disputes, in order to wreak vengeance against the husband and relatives of the husband, certain wives initiate criminal proceedings on the strength of vague and omnibus allegations against the parents, sisters, brothers and other relatives of the husband with ulterior motive to put them under the veil of prosecution involving non-bailable offences and to face the ordeal of criminal prosecution and trial by the parents, sisters, brothers and other relatives of the husband, so as to malign and defame their image in the society.

In such cases, it is the duty of the court to analyse materials available when quashment is sought whether the allegations specifically state anything dealt under Section 2024:KER:72715 2024:KER:588 498A so as to prosecute the accused for the said offences, by subjecting themselves for trial.
The cases where no specific allegations to go for trial, prima facie, such cases shall be quashed by the High Court by invoking power under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.

At the same time, when specific allegations pointing out the overt acts which would attract the offence under Section 498A could be seen, prima Prasanna vs State Of Kerala on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39290669/
4 facie, from the prosecution case, such cases shall not be quashed.

sentences.text: 11. Here, there is specific allegation against the 1 st accused, who is not a party in this petition.

Coming to the allegations against the 2 nd accused, the defacto complainant stated in her statement that, the 2nd accused/1st petitioner herein accompanied the defacto complainant and 1st accused and during their stay at Bangalore and she used to make problems on saying that there was a practice in Palakkad to give chain to the husband during marriage.
Thereafter, the parents of the defacto complainant given gold chain having 2.5 sovereigns to the 1st accused.

It is further alleged that, the 2 nd accused 2024:KER:72715 2024:KER:588 demanded more gold ornaments from the defacto complainant on asserting that the sisters of the 1 st accused were given 40 sovereigns of gold ornaments at the time of their marriage.

12. But the allegations against accused Nos. 3 to 5 are not specific and the same are general and vague in nature, raised with a view to implicate them in this crime, which was registered on 22.12.2021, that is, after five years of the alleged occurrence.
13. Since, there is specific allegation as against the 2nd accused/1st petitioner, quashment of the proceedings against the 1st petitioner/2nd accused is not liable to be quashed.

At the same time,
only general, vague and sweeping allegations without bringing on record any specific instance of cruelty at the instance of the petitioners 2 to 4 herein/accused Nos.3 to 5.
Therefore, the case against accused Nos. 3 to 5/petitioners 2 to 4 is liable to be quashed.
14. In the result, this petition stands allowed in part.
The quashment prayer at the option of the 1 st petitioner/2nd 2024:KER:72715 2024:KER:588 accused stands dismissed.

All further proceedings in C.C. No.298/2022 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-II, Palakkad, as against petitioners 2 to 4/accused Nos.3 to 5, stand quashed, with liberty to the trial court to proceed with trial against accused Nos. 1 and 2.
